title: BalancerPoolerV2.migrateMint unbounded per-unit mintFor loop scales O(amount) and can become un-callable for large id-4 holders
description:
migrateMint accepts `uint256 amount` and executes `for (uint256 i; i < amount; ++i) { INFTMinterV2(minter).mintFor(NEW_NFT_INDEX, mintRecipient); }`. Each iteration is a full external call into NFTMinterV2.mintFor, which: validates `authorizedMinters[msg.sender]`, validates `configs[index].dispatcher != address(0)`, executes OZ ERC1155 `_mint` (one balance SSTORE for the recipient, one supply SSTORE for the id, one TransferSingle event, and the receiver-acceptance-check call) and emits a ClaimMintedFor event. Realistic per-iteration gas: ~35k-60k cold/warm depending on the recipient code and existing balance slots. The test suite documents the worst case as N=41 (test_migrateMint_multiNFTLoop_41), so the project has implicitly assumed migration cohorts will be ~tens, not hundreds.

If the original id-4 distribution concentrated NFTs on a treasury, a market maker, or a single power user (>~500 id-4 NFTs in one wallet), that holder cannot complete migration in a single transaction on Ethereum mainnet without exceeding the ~30M block gas limit. The migration is all-or-nothing per call: if the loop runs out of gas mid-flight, the entire tx reverts and the holder is unable to migrate. The only workaround is for the holder to split id-4 across multiple wallets via safeBatchTransferFrom prior to migrating, paying gas premiums and exposing themselves to L1 transfer-tracing.

The rounding direction is also unhelpful: there is no `migrateMintPartial(uint256 amount, ...)` to migrate a slice of the holder's balance — `amount` must equal the holder's intended migrate count, and the holder has to manage the chunking themselves at the calling-tx level.

This duplicates the same scaling pattern flagged in report-6 RAW-005 (NFTMigrator.migrate) for the V1->V2 case. The fix is identical: add a `mintForBatch(index, recipient, quantity)` to NFTMinterV2 that calls ERC1155 `_mint(recipient, index, quantity, "")` once, and have migrateMint call it once.
exploit_path:
1. Alice (or a treasury / market maker that accumulated id-4 NFTs during the original BalancerPoolerV2 lifetime) holds 800 id-4 NFTs.
2. Alice calls migrateMint(800, alice). The burn succeeds (one cheap ERC1155 _burn with quantity=800). Then the loop begins.
3. At ~40k gas per mintFor iteration, the loop alone budgets to ~32M gas — over the mainnet block gas limit.
4. The transaction reverts. Alice's 800 id-4 are un-burned (revert rolls back), so she has not lost NFTs. But she also cannot migrate via this entry point.
5. Alice's only on-chain workaround is to split her id-4 across N fresh wallets via safeBatchTransferFrom and call migrateMint from each — costing N times the migration gas plus the split-transfer gas. For a custodian / institutional holder this may be operationally infeasible (compliance / signing-policy constraints on creating fresh wallets just to migrate).

The attack is a UX / availability failure, not theft. But it stratifies the migration: small holders migrate freely, large holders are excluded.
mainnet_realism_check: Mainnet block gas limit is ~30M. ERC1155 _mint cost is well documented. The test suite explicitly tests N=41 as a stated worst case, indicating the team has not yet stress-tested the loop against large concentrations.
recommendation: Replace the per-unit loop with a single batched mint. Add `mintForBatch(uint256 index, address recipient, uint256 quantity)` to NFTMinterV2 (gated by `authorizedMinters[msg.sender]`) that calls `_mint(recipient, index, quantity, "")`, then rewrite migrateMint to: `INFTMinterV2(minter).burn(msg.sender, OLD_NFT_ID, amount); INFTMinterV2(minter).mintForBatch(NEW_NFT_INDEX, mintRecipient, amount);`. This converts the migration from O(amount) to O(1) external calls. Alternatively, accept `amount` as a chunk size and let large holders split across multiple txs — but then document that explicitly and emit a partial-migration event.
